pillar_reactions.evidence: The most engaged pillar reaction in the batch — he interrupted the presentation three times with substantive mechanics questions rather than accepting it. First: 'from what I've explained about my current routine, would this come in to replace what I do today completely, or would it be replacing parts of my current training?' (answer: it replaces the weights, not the boxing). Second: 'would this training, if it's replacing the current strength component of my training, would it still allow me to maintain a level of strength?' Third: 'how does it work in terms of ensuring I'm doing things properly?... have I got the right form?' He also endorsed the core premise before the rep finished making it — when told bodybuilding does not build functional strength he said 'I'm like a poster boy for it right now.' Classified clarifying rather than enthusiastic because the questions were risk-testing, not appetite.

Landed cleanly because the rep had already done the diagnostic work in the baseline and could point at a specific finding rather than deliver a generic framework — the hidden sugar in two daily office biscuits, two-sugar coffees and sweetened protein shakes inside a diet that looked clean. The prospect had already reached the same conclusion himself ('maybe it's the quality of your life having, so I think the sugar associated with either the protein shake, or the couple of coffees'). He confirmed the eight-hour window was close to what he already does ('Yes, a version of that, yes') and closed the section with 'Nope. That sounds pretty straightforward.' NOTE: the rep asserted a single biscuit is 'probably around 500 calories', which is roughly five to ten times a realistic figure, and used it to explain the weight gain.

Volunteered a positive reaction and then extended the argument himself: 'I like the idea of the app. I think, irrespective of how disciplined you are, having external accountability just keeps you... I call it the 80-20 rule, right? Even if you're doing something in person, if you're still going to slack 20% of the time, and if having external accountability allows you to fix that 20%...' followed by 'you never regret the workout. It's always the ones that you don't.' Notably the rep opened this section by conceding the pillar was not really for him — 'you seem like a very disciplined guy, so you don't need hand-holding' — and repositioned it around technique acquisition, which was the correct read; the prospect then bought the accountability argument anyway on his own terms. He also identified where he actually needs it: 'I'm less worried about the workout element, because I enjoy that part. It's the discipline with the diet.'

anchors.raw: The guy who I spoke to yesterday... So the idea that I asked him how much is going to be, he goes, it's between 1 and 6, but he goes, the next call will tell you more. So it's come out at 6.
anchors.note: The most damaging anchor in the batch and it was created internally, not by a competitor. The setter Derek told this prospect the price was somewhere between one and six thousand, which means he spent a day expecting a possible $1,000 entry point and then experienced $6,000 as the ceiling of a range rather than as the price of the thing. His own phrasing — 'So it's come out at 6' — is the language of a bad outcome in a negotiation, not of a value assessment. Read alongside the $3,000 tier improvised on the smanian call the same day, this raises a live question about what price points the market is being told exist.

anchors.raw: if I was paying for a personal trainer would I be paying that kind of money? It seems like it's a bit more then what I'd be paying for a personal trainer if I was doing an hour a week, couple of hours a week. So I think it's at the top end of that.
anchors.note: He performed the comparison out loud and reached an unfavourable conclusion, then rebutted himself unprompted — 'But also, this is something different, right? If I was going to just pay for a personal trainer, I would have done it.' The rep contributed nothing to either side. Third unanswered cheaper-alternative anchor in this batch; the prospects keep supplying the counter-argument the playbook does not.

anchors.raw: So as I mentioned, the full transformation takes six months, right? So for that period to work with Trevor, the full investment is 6K USD. Which is in pounds, I don't know, 4,800.-ish, yeah.
anchors.note: The rep converted to sterling off the cuff and with an explicit disclaimer of uncertainty. The lower nominal figure softens the ask, but it creates a real risk: a UK buyer may anchor to £4,800 and be billed a USD amount that moves with the exchange rate. No contract currency, no FX basis and no date were stated.

anchors.raw: So what's that 1,000 a month, basically? Is that right? Is that how he's working it out?
anchors.note: Fifth prospect in this batch to convert $6,000 into a monthly figure within seconds of hearing it, and the fourth to land on $1,000/month. The rep again defaulted to 'Usually guys just put it on a credit card and pay it up front' rather than owning or reframing the monthly lens. At this frequency it is not a coincidence — buyers are pricing this as a subscription and the pitch is not meeting them there.

anchors.raw: I can sit on a vertical leg press machine and do 300 kilos because my legs are strong ... I train every day. I'll do one day weights, one day boxing, one day weights, one day boxing.
anchors.competitor: his own gym membership and twenty years of self-directed training
anchors.note: He has access, equipment, discipline and daily consistency already. Nothing in the offer's convenience or motivation framing applies to him, so the entire premium rests on method and technique transfer. The rep recognised this and repositioned accountability toward technique, which was correct — but it narrows the value story to one pillar.

anchors.raw: That's when I come across some of the videos on Insta, where I'm looking at some of kettlebell workouts, and I was like, okay, this is really interesting, because in terms of functional strength, there's not a lot
anchors.note: Arrived through Instagram content, was pre-briefed by the setter, and had already tried a kettlebell once out of curiosity. Modality interest was established before the call and never needed to be sold — which is exactly why the price anchor the setter set was the only thing left doing damage.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that replacing twenty years of bodybuilding with kettlebells will not cost him the strength he has built
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked this directly and it is his central commercial risk. The answer was reassurance plus a mention of pull-ups, dips and push-ups, with no evidence, no case example and no progression model — delivered immediately before the rep suggested starting at a 16 kg bell to a man who leg presses 300 kg. Whether the programme preserves absolute strength in an experienced lifter is genuinely unestablished from this call.

unmet_demand.want: Assessment and correction of restricted hip mobility, which he identifies as the root cause of weak glutes, weak lower back and knee pain
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is his primary stated reason for being on the call. The offer promises generic five-to-ten-minute mobility protocols for 'any stiffness, any issues that you have with your hips, lower back, shoulders'. Nobody assessed the hip, asked how long it has been restricted, asked whether it has ever been examined, or established whether a mobility protocol is the right intervention for what he is describing.

unmet_demand.want: Visible abs in his forties, having never achieved them even at his target weight of 78 kg
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised this precisely and with a caveat that matters — 'even at that level, you couldn't see my abs' — meaning weight loss alone has already been proven insufficient for this goal. The rep folded it into general fat loss toward 78 kg and never engaged with the fact that the prospect has run that experiment and it failed.

unmet_demand.want: A clear price expectation before reaching the closing call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The setter gave a range of 'between 1 and 6' and deferred the answer to the next call. The information exists and is fixed; the process chose not to state it, which cost the closer his first two minutes after the reveal and framed the real price as the top of a range.

unmet_demand.want: A way to commit to a considered decision without deciding on the call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He is a deliberate decision-maker who said plainly that impulse is not how he operates and that even a $2,000 price would not change that. There is no deposit, no place-holding mechanism, no start date and no cohort — nothing that lets a buyer like this convert intent into commitment while still taking his day to think.
